info.title: Wallet Ledger
info.description: INR wallet backend with bearer authentication and explicit SQL. Every POST requires a UUID Idempotency-Key, scoped to the authenticated caller. Identical retries return the saved status and JSON body with Idempotent-Replay: true. Changing the endpoint, resource or validated body with the same key returns 422. Concurrent duplicates wait up to five seconds; a still-busy key returns 409. Business failures are saved; validation, authentication and infrastructure failures are not.

get.description:
Newest first. Follow next_cursor for stable seek pagination during new postings.

Offset remains available for numbered pages. Cursor and nonzero offset cannot be combined.
Cursors are untrusted seek positions bound to a wallet, not credentials or snapshot tokens.

Opening and closing ledger balance, gross credits/debits and transfer count.

Dates are inclusive UTC dates based on entry creation time. One read-only Repeatable Read
snapshot supplies all totals. Held transfers have no entries and contribute nothing.
Reversals appear as new movements; cached account balances and LLMs are not used.

post.description:
Answer one of four supported questions from posted movements in the user's own wallets.

Dates are inclusive UTC dates. Values are gross posted movements, including top-ups and
reversals; counts deduplicate transfers touching two of the same user's wallets.
At most 1000 contributing movements; narrow wider results. No ledger rows reach the
statement-intent provider. The default provider is an offline mock, not a learned model.

Idempotent-Replay.description: false for the initial response; true for a saved response

post.description:
Post a peer payment or withdrawal from an owned wallet. Admins may top up or charge fees.

Amounts are integer paise. Top-up needs destination_account_id; withdrawal and fee need
source_account_id; peer needs both. System endpoints are resolved by the server.

finding_count counts raw invariant violations; problem_count compares ledger and caches
against posted business events. A single damaged entry can violate several invariants.
The run returns passed, failed (integrity problems), or error (checks could not complete).
